title.narrative: Enhancing Nature-based Solutions and Green Infrastructure networks in urban and peri-urban areas in Chile

description.narrative: NbS and GI offer multiple environmental, social, and economic benefits. They are an approach that seeks to solve urban problems by leveraging the advantages and conditions that nature uses to solve them, addressing territorial, social, economic, and environmental challenges. The main social benefits of NbS and GI are directly related to people's health and well-being, improving the sense of community and social integration, contributing to gender equity and quality of life, providing recreational opportunities for communities, and promoting the reduction of vulnerability to climate change. At the national and local levels, the Project's social and economic benefits will contribute to promoting and strengthening the implementation of these solutions, improving living conditions in urban areas by generating access to green spaces, clean and conserved urban ecosystems, awareness-raising and education activities, and social integration. Furthermore, these benefits will provide opportunities for urban neighborhoods and communities to strengthen community NbS and GI networks and ensure their sustainability over time. The economic benefits generated by NbS and GI networks include a contribution to cost-effectiveness analysis of interventions in selected urban areas, cost-reductions due to the reduction of flooding and other climate-related threats, and employment opportunities. In this last aspect, they promote green jobs associated with activities and businesses involved sustainable urban development, environmental preservation, ecosystem restoration, tree planting, and generating business opportunities and local partnerships around circular economy and urban agri-food systems for food security and nutrition, contributing to the project’s objective of promoting the health and well being of people. According to the ILO definition, green jobs are "decent jobs that contribute to preserving and restoring the environment, whether in traditional sectors such as manufacturing and construction, or in emerging sectors such as renewable energy and energy efficiency." On the other hand, the ILO definition of decent work "means the opportunity to access productive employment generating a fair income, workplace security and social protection for all, improved prospects for personal development and social integration, freedom for individuals to express their opinions, organize and participate in decisions that affect their lives, and equality of opportunity and treatment for all, women and men." On the other hand, the SDG 8 on Decent employment and Economic Growth recommends integrating policies on decent urban employment, referring to productive work, offers a fair income, provides security, social protection, and opportunities for development within urban areas. It also includes freedom of expression, organization, and participation in decisions affecting workers. This approach is also applicable to rural areas, as recommended by FAO, and can contribute to strengthening urban-rural linkages.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

To expand and integrate nature-based solutions (NbS) and green infrastructure (GI) in cities and peri-urban areas in Chile to promote the conservation and restoration of biodiversity, mitigate climate change, and promote the health and wellbeing of people in urban areas
